title: TTNN cheat sheet for a decoder port

roots.tt_metal: tt-metal source tree at the coder image's pinned commit (python bindings, C++ nanobind files and ttnn python)

intro: Each signature was checked against the tt-metal tree the coder image is built from. Arguments not listed here do not exist. `python3 stages/2/stage_tools.py cheat NAME` prints one entry.

entries.name: ttnn.from_torch
entries.signature: ttnn.from_torch(tensor, dtype=None, layout=None, device=None, memory_config=None, mesh_mapper=None)
entries.notes: Host torch tensor to device. Weights go in TILE_LAYOUT; token ids for an embedding go in ROW_MAJOR_LAYOUT as uint32. On a mesh pass a mesh_mapper or the tensor lands on one device.

entries.name: ttnn.to_torch
entries.notes: Device tensor to torch. With a mesh the composer joins the per-device shards; replicated tensors then repeat, so take the first copy. The result is padded to tiles: slice to the real length.

entries.name: ttnn.as_tensor
entries.signature: ttnn.as_tensor(tensor, dtype=None, layout=None, device=None, memory_config=None, mesh_mapper=None, cache_file_name=None)
entries.usage: w = ttnn.as_tensor(w_torch, dtype=ttnn.bfloat16, device=mesh_device, layout=ttnn.TILE_LAYOUT, memory_config=ttnn.DRAM_MEMORY_CONFIG)
entries.notes: Like from_torch, and can cache the converted weight on disk with cache_file_name.

entries.name: ttnn.to_layout
entries.notes: Changes TILE_LAYOUT and ROW_MAJOR_LAYOUT. Matmul, rms_norm and attention need TILE_LAYOUT; embedding ids and reshapes of odd shapes need ROW_MAJOR_LAYOUT.

entries.name: ttnn.typecast
entries.notes: Changes dtype on the device. Rotary embedding and attention want bfloat16 inputs; bfloat8_b is for weights and some activations.

entries.name: ttnn.reshape
entries.notes: Shapes are 4-D by convention in the reference ports: (1, 1, tokens, features). The last two dims are padded to 32.

entries.name: ttnn.transpose
entries.notes: Swaps two dims.

entries.name: ttnn.concat
entries.notes: Joins a list of tensors along one dim.

entries.name: ttnn.multiply
entries.notes: Elementwise product; b may be a Python scalar. add, subtract and silu are called the same way.

entries.name: ttnn.silu
entries.notes: Activation for the gated MLP: down(silu(gate) * up).

entries.name: ttnn.deallocate
entries.notes: Frees a device tensor you no longer need. Needed inside a layer loop on a small chip.

entries.name: ttnn.TILE_LAYOUT
entries.notes: 32x32 tile layout. Dtypes: ttnn.bfloat16, ttnn.bfloat8_b, ttnn.uint32, ttnn.int32.

entries.name: ttnn.ROW_MAJOR_LAYOUT
entries.notes: Layout for token ids. Pair it with ttnn.uint32.

entries.name: ttnn.embedding
entries.signature: ttnn.embedding(input_tensor, weight, *, padding_idx=None, layout=None, embeddings_type=None, dtype=None, memory_config=None)
entries.notes: ids are uint32 ROW_MAJOR; the weight is the [vocab, hidden] table in ROW_MAJOR. The keyword is `weight`; `weights` is an error. Without layout=TILE_LAYOUT the output is row major.

entries.name: ttnn.linear
entries.signature: ttnn.linear(input_tensor_a, input_tensor_b, *, bias=None, transpose_a=False, transpose_b=False, memory_config=None, dtype=None, program_config=None, activation=None, compute_kernel_config=None, core_grid=None)
entries.usage: y = ttnn.linear(x, w, bias=b, dtype=ttnn.bfloat16, compute_kernel_config=ck, memory_config=ttnn.DRAM_MEMORY_CONFIG)
entries.notes: x @ w (+ bias). The torch Linear weight is [out, in]: transpose it once at load (w_torch.T) or pass transpose_b=True. With no program_config the op picks one; start there.

entries.name: ttnn.matmul
entries.signature: ttnn.matmul(input_tensor_a, input_tensor_b, *, transpose_a=False, transpose_b=False, memory_config=None, dtype=None, program_config=None, activation=None, compute_kernel_config=None, core_grid=None)
entries.notes: Same as linear without bias. Batched matmul broadcasts the leading dims; both inputs must be TILE_LAYOUT.

entries.name: ttnn.MatmulMultiCoreReuseMultiCastProgramConfig
entries.signature: ttnn.MatmulMultiCoreReuseMultiCastProgramConfig(compute_with_storage_grid_size, in0_block_w, out_subblock_h, out_subblock_w, per_core_M, per_core_N, transpose_mcast, fused_activation, fuse_batch)
entries.usage: pc = ttnn.MatmulMultiCoreReuseMultiCastProgramConfig(compute_with_storage_grid_size=(8, 8), in0_block_w=1, out_subblock_h=1, out_subblock_w=1, per_core_M=1, per_core_N=56, transpose_mcast=False, fused_activation=None, fuse_batch=False)
entries.notes: Program config for a large matmul (prefill, interleaved). per_core_M and per_core_N count tiles per core; out_subblock_h * out_subblock_w <= 4. Skip it in a first port.

entries.name: ttnn.MatmulMultiCoreReuseMultiCast1DProgramConfig
entries.signature: ttnn.MatmulMultiCoreReuseMultiCast1DProgramConfig(compute_with_storage_grid_size, in0_block_w, out_subblock_h, out_subblock_w, per_core_M, per_core_N, fuse_batch, fused_activation, mcast_in0)
entries.usage: pc = ttnn.MatmulMultiCoreReuseMultiCast1DProgramConfig(compute_with_storage_grid_size=(8, 8), in0_block_w=2, out_subblock_h=1, out_subblock_w=4, per_core_M=1, per_core_N=8, fuse_batch=True, fused_activation=None, mcast_in0=True)
entries.notes: Program config for decode, where M is one tile row (batch up to 32).

entries.name: ttnn.WormholeComputeKernelConfig
entries.notes: Precision of a matmul or norm. HiFi4 with fp32 accumulation is the safe choice while matching the CPU reference; lower fidelity comes after the check passes. Blackhole uses the same class.

entries.name: ttnn.rms_norm
entries.signature: ttnn.rms_norm(input_tensor, *, epsilon=1e-12, weight=None, bias=None, residual_input_tensor=None, memory_config=None, program_config=None, compute_kernel_config=None)
entries.notes: Set epsilon from the config; the default 1e-12 is rarely right. A ROW_MAJOR weight needs last dim 32 ([1, 1, hidden/32, 32]); a TILE weight needs the input's last dim. If the reference adds 1 to the weight, add it at load. The keywords are epsilon and weight.

entries.name: ttnn.softmax
entries.notes: Use numeric_stable=True for attention scores built by hand.

entries.name: ttnn.experimental.rotary_embedding_llama
entries.signature: ttnn.experimental.rotary_embedding_llama(input_tensor, cos_cache, sin_cache, trans_mat, is_decode_mode=False, memory_config=None, compute_kernel_config=None)
entries.notes: Rotation for the Llama pairing (rotate_half layout). cos and sin are [1, 1, seq, head_dim]; trans_mat is a 32x32 transformation matrix built once (see rope.py). The op rotates a whole head: when partial_rotary_factor is below 1, split the head, rotate the first head_dim * factor values and concat the rest.

entries.name: ttnn.experimental.rotary_embedding_hf
entries.notes: Rotation in the HF layout (first half and second half). Use this when the reference calls rotate_half on the checkpoint's own layout and you did not permute the q and k weights.

entries.name: ttnn.experimental.nlp_create_qkv_heads
entries.usage: q, k, v = ttnn.experimental.nlp_create_qkv_heads(xqkv, num_heads=n_heads, num_kv_heads=n_kv, transpose_k_heads=False, memory_config=ttnn.DRAM_MEMORY_CONFIG)
entries.notes: Splits a fused [1, 1, seq, (nh + 2*nkv)*hd] qkv tensor into q [1, nh, seq, hd], k and v [1, nkv, seq, hd]. Prefill form. Set transpose_k_heads=False to keep k as [.., seq, hd].

entries.name: ttnn.experimental.nlp_create_qkv_heads_decode
entries.usage: q, k, v = ttnn.experimental.nlp_create_qkv_heads_decode(xqkv, num_heads=n_heads, num_kv_heads=n_kv, memory_config=mc)
entries.notes: Decode form of the head split (batch in dim 1). Takes a sharded input in the fast path.

entries.name: ttnn.experimental.nlp_concat_heads
entries.notes: [1, nh, seq, hd] back to [1, 1, seq, nh*hd] before the output projection.

entries.name: ttnn.transformer.scaled_dot_product_attention
entries.signature: ttnn.transformer.scaled_dot_product_attention(input_tensor_q, input_tensor_k, input_tensor_v, *, attn_mask=None, is_causal=True, scale=None, sliding_window_size=None, memory_config=None, program_config=None, compute_kernel_config=None)
entries.notes: Prefill attention. k and v may have fewer heads than q (grouped query): do not repeat them yourself. Give only one of attn_mask and is_causal=True. The mask keyword is attn_mask. The sequence must be padded to a multiple of 32.

entries.name: ttnn.transformer.scaled_dot_product_attention_decode
entries.signature: ttnn.transformer.scaled_dot_product_attention_decode(input_tensor_q, input_tensor_k, input_tensor_v, *, is_causal=True, attn_mask=None, cur_pos=None, cur_pos_tensor=None, scale=None, sliding_window_size=None, memory_config=None, program_config=None, compute_kernel_config=None)
entries.notes: Decode attention over a dense KV cache. q is [1, batch, heads, hd]. cur_pos_tensor is an int32 device tensor with each user's current position.

entries.name: ttnn.transformer.paged_scaled_dot_product_attention_decode
entries.signature: ttnn.transformer.paged_scaled_dot_product_attention_decode(input_tensor_q, input_tensor_k, input_tensor_v, page_table_tensor, *, is_causal=True, attn_mask=None, cur_pos_tensor=None, scale=None, sliding_window_size=None, memory_config=None, program_config=None, compute_kernel_config=None)
entries.usage: o = ttnn.transformer.paged_scaled_dot_product_attention_decode(q, keys, values, page_table_tensor=page_table, cur_pos_tensor=pos, scale=head_dim ** -0.5)
entries.notes: Decode attention over a paged cache (what vLLM serving uses). Keys and values are the paged cache tensors.

entries.name: ttnn.experimental.paged_update_cache
entries.signature: ttnn.experimental.paged_update_cache(cache_tensor, input_tensor, *, update_idxs=None, update_idxs_tensor=None, share_cache=None, page_table=None, batch_offset=0, compute_kernel_config=None)
entries.notes: Writes one new token per user into the paged cache at its position. Call it for keys and for values. pos is an int32 device tensor.

entries.name: ttnn.experimental.paged_fill_cache
entries.notes: Writes a whole prefill's keys or values into the paged cache. The cache must be reset or overwritten at the start of each request.

entries.name: ttnn.fill_cache
entries.notes: Dense (not paged) cache fill for one user. Use this in a first port that has no page table.

entries.name: ttnn.argmax
entries.notes: Index of the largest value along dim; the output is UINT32. TILE input works for bfloat16 and float32 on the last dim (single core); ROW_MAJOR runs multicore. A port returns logits to the check, so use this only for a serving path.

entries.name: ttnn.topk
entries.signature: ttnn.topk(input_tensor, k, dim=-1, largest=True, sorted=True, memory_config=None)
entries.notes: Returns (values, indices). The input is TILE on the device; N*C*H must be a multiple of 32 and the last dim is padded to tiles.

entries.name: ttnn.sampling
entries.signature: ttnn.sampling(input_values_tensor, input_indices_tensor, *, k, p, temp, seed=None)
entries.usage: tok = ttnn.sampling(vals, idx, k=k_t, p=p_t, temp=inv_t, seed=1234)
entries.notes: Samples an index from the output of topk: softmax over input_values_tensor, then top-k and top-p, then multinomial. k and p are tensors, temp is a tensor holding 1/T, seed is an int. Inputs are bfloat16 TILE.

sections.title: Mesh and collectives (more than one chip)

entries.name: ttnn.open_mesh_device
entries.notes: The check opens the mesh and passes it to `load`; a port does not open one. Shown so you know the shape: (1, N) for N chips in a row.

entries.name: ttnn.ReplicateTensorToMesh
entries.notes: Mapper for from_torch: every chip gets the full tensor.

entries.name: ttnn.ShardTensorToMesh
entries.notes: Mapper for from_torch: dim is split across the chips. Column-parallel weights shard the output dim; row-parallel shard the input dim.

entries.name: ttnn.ConcatMeshToTensor
entries.notes: Composer for to_torch: joins the per-chip shards along dim.

entries.name: ttnn.get_device_tensors
entries.notes: The list of per-chip tensors of a mesh tensor; to_torch each one to read a single chip.

entries.name: ttnn.all_gather
entries.signature: ttnn.all_gather(input_tensor, dim, *, cluster_axis=None, memory_config=None, num_links=None, topology=None)
entries.notes: Joins the shards of a mesh tensor along dim on every chip. Use after a column-parallel matmul whose output feeds a replicated op.

entries.name: ttnn.reduce_scatter
entries.signature: ttnn.reduce_scatter(input_tensor, dim, *, cluster_axis=None, memory_config=None, num_links=None, topology=None)
entries.notes: Sums the partial results of a row-parallel matmul and leaves each chip one slice. Pair with all_gather to get a replicated tensor.

entries.name: ttnn.all_reduce
entries.notes: Sum of the partial results on every chip (reduce_scatter then all_gather in one call). Use it after a row-parallel matmul when the next op needs the full tensor.

entries.name: ttnn.experimental.all_gather_async
entries.signature: ttnn.experimental.all_gather_async(input_tensor, dim, *, multi_device_global_semaphore, num_links=1, memory_config=None, topology=None, cluster_axis=None)
entries.usage: g = ttnn.experimental.all_gather_async(x, dim=3, multi_device_global_semaphore=sem, num_links=1, cluster_axis=1)
entries.notes: The asynchronous form the reference ports use inside traces. It needs global semaphores made once (ttnn.create_global_semaphore). A first port uses the blocking ttnn.all_gather.

mistakes.symptom: `NotImplementedError: prefill not implemented yet` at the first check (run 16).
mistakes.fix: The skeleton raises this in load, prefill, decode_step and close. Write all four before the check runs, even if decode_step first calls prefill on the whole sequence.

mistakes.symptom: `Expected size for first two dimensions of batch2 tensor to be: [6, 32] but got: [6, 6]` (run 18).
mistakes.fix: A matmul between grouped heads of different counts (6 value heads, 2 key heads). Read linear_num_key_heads and linear_num_value_heads with `facts`, repeat the key heads to the value-head count, and print the shapes before each matmul.

mistakes.symptom: `The size of tensor a (32) must match the size of tensor b (8) at non-singleton dimension 3`.
mistakes.fix: Rotary applies to head_dim * partial_rotary_factor (8 of 32 here). Rotate the first part of the head and leave the rest.

mistakes.symptom: `Expected 4-dimensional input for 4-dimensional weight [320, 1, 1, 4], but got 3-dimensional input`.
mistakes.fix: A causal depthwise conv: use torch conv1d with a [C, 1, K] weight, input [B, C, T], left padding K-1 and groups=C. Do not mix a 4-D conv2d weight with a 3-D input.

mistakes.symptom: `SyntaxError: unterminated string literal` at init, after a long write_file.
mistakes.fix: The reply hit the token cap in the middle of the file. Write the port in two or three smaller files or functions and re-read the end of the file after each write.

mistakes.symptom: Top-1 agreement 0.5625 against the 0.85 bar with every op running (runs 16 and 18).
mistakes.fix: Run `stage_tools.py layer-diff` (define layer_outputs in port_model.py) and fix the first layer that differs before touching decode.

mistakes.symptom: A guessed argument that does not exist: `weights=` for embedding, `eps=` or `gamma=` for rms_norm, `mask=` for attention, `bias=` for matmul.
mistakes.fix: The names are weight, epsilon and weight, attn_mask, and bias only on linear.
mistakes.seen_in: CAD benchmark pattern; checked against the tree

mistakes.symptom: `ttnn.conv1d` as a depthwise convolution with dilation above 1 returns a wrong result (PCC 0.2) and raises no error (issue 338).
mistakes.fix: Write the short convolution as shifted multiply-adds: for a kernel of 4 and dilation 3, y = sum_k w[k] * shift(x, (3-k)*3), then silu.

mistakes.symptom: A 4-chip mesh open times out in fabric router sync (run 17, issue 487).
mistakes.fix: A chip link is unhealthy. The port cannot fix it: report it in handoff.json and let the supervisor reset the chips.
